name: Build a target account list by size and funding stage with Bounce Watch in Airtable

parameters.content:
## Build a target account list by size and funding stage with Bounce Watch in Airtable

Bounce Watch tells you what just happened at a company and when — funding, senior hires, new offices, customer wins and partnerships, each carrying its own date. What the API covers: bouncewatch.com/products/data-enrichment-api

An ideal customer profile is only useful once it is a list of names. This workflow turns a size band, a funding stage and a country into rows in Airtable, refreshed every week.

### How it works

A weekly schedule starts the run. A Settings node holds the profile — country, headcount range and funding stage — in one place. The Bounce Watch node searches the index for companies that fit, and returns them as a single result, so a split node turns that into one item per company before Airtable receives it. Each row carries the name, domain, country, headcount, stage and a link to the profile.

### Setup

1. Get an API key at bouncewatch.com/register/api. It is free, no card, and every new account starts with 2,500 credits. Paste it into the Bounce Watch credential.
2. Fill in the profile in Target profile. Leave a field empty to drop that constraint.
3. Connect your Airtable credential and choose the base and table on the last node.

A funding stage narrows twice: once by the stage, and once by the companies whose stage we hold. A short list is as likely to be a gap in what we know as a fact about the market.

### Customization tips

Add a founding-year range to the filters for an age band. Point the last node at a spreadsheet or your CRM instead if that is where your target list lives.

## Describe the target

Country, headcount band, funding stage.
An empty field drops that constraint.

## Search and split

The search returns one result set.
Split turns it into one item per company.

## Write to Airtable

One row per company.
